asi.evidence: Forty warmed local-hit runs measured 26.30 ms median with 1.00 ms standard deviation after the full workspace and 241 command-line examples passed.

asi.evidence: Mimalloc measured 25.75 ms in its stable repeat, while the immediately rebuilt system allocator measured 25.13 ms. A separate allocator run was badly distorted by system load.
asi.hypothesis: Page-local allocator sharding helps concurrent workloads, but Once now keeps this fast path mostly on one thread and does not recover the added allocator startup cost.
asi.next: Keep the system allocator and target repeated logging setup, parsing, and remote request dependencies instead.

asi.evidence: Twenty clean-client remote hits measured 176.89 ms median and 175.53 ms mean with a 6.02 ms standard deviation.
asi.hypothesis: Per-request blocking authentication and duplicate initial channel connections add avoidable remote-path latency.
asi.next: Resolve authentication once per process and make channel initialization single-flight.

asi.evidence: After an outlier run under system load, the stable repeat measured 173.55 ms median versus the 176.89 ms baseline. Two earlier repeats of the same fast path measured 174.85 and 175.03 ms.
asi.hypothesis: Resolving authentication once, making channel establishment single-flight, and avoiding a throwaway single-endpoint probe removes blocking-pool handoffs and duplicate transport setup.
asi.next: Move validated host tool identity caching out of disposable workspace action state, then optimize prelude selection.

asi.evidence: Two controlled remote runs measured 143.42 and 148.71 ms median versus the 176.89 ms baseline. The stable repeat improved median latency by 15.9 percent.
asi.hypothesis: Host executable paths and safe version probes are machine identity, not disposable action state. Retaining them avoids toolchain-manager and Node process startup after an action-cache clear.
asi.next: Replace the full prelude source scan with indexed target-kind metadata and return to local-hit measurement.
